name: Orangey Red
lede: Orangey Red is a descriptive name for a vivid red leaning to orange, a plain phrase rather than a pigment or a dye.

sections.title: A plain-English gloss
sections.body:
Orangey Red entered our sources through the 2010 xkcd survey, where volunteers named screen colors in their own words [1]. It is not a historic dye or pigment name [1]. Our library places the swatch in the ISCC-NBS block called vivid reddish orange, 4.8 units away on the CIEDE2000 scale [1].

Books use the phrase as a gloss, a way to explain another word. Paterson's dictionary defines lava-red as an intense orangey-red, salmon red as an orangey-red, and saffron as an orangey-red or a deep yellow [2][3]. It also uses the same words for bilirubin, the pigment in bile [4].

sections.title: A phrase that stretches
sections.body: The dictionary applies the same two-word description to things that are called red and yellow in other entries, which shows how loosely the middle of the spectrum is named [2][3]. It glosses flame-yellow, for one, as a bright orangey-red [5]. Where the books disagree on a name, the safer guide is the neighbor: this swatch sits between [[orange-red]] and plain [[red]], with [[orange]] close behind.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a color near this swatch appears in only 6 works, or 0.03 per cent, which is rarer than 73 per cent of the named colors [6]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a color match is not a pigment test [6].
